title: For the UPSC CSE mains, should the initial days of my answer writing practice be within strict time limits of 11 and 7 minutes? Does the speed and handwriting improve as we write more answers?
reason: The user is asking about the mechanics of answer writing (speed, time limits, and handwriting improvement), which directly relates to the 'Mains Answer Writing Framework' and the need for structured, high-yield content to manage time effectively.

matched_note.title: UPSC CSE Mains Answer Writing Framework: Structure, Committee Quotes & Data Points

drafted_comment:
The real issue here is trying to run before you can walk. In the initial days, focus on content quality over raw speed. If you rush now, you'll just produce messy, low-value answers that don't help you improve.

Here is a better way to start:

1. Focus on the '4-Anchor' structure first: Ensure every answer has a Constitutional basis, hard data, a specific committee quote, and a clear way forward.
2. Quality over Speed: Spend the first few weeks perfecting the structure of 10 and 15-markers. Speed and handwriting will naturally improve as your mental map of the syllabus becomes clearer.
3. Use Model Answers: Compare your attempts with high-scoring structures to see where you are losing time or points.\n
